findings.title: Campaign policy precedence
findings.sourceIssue: F004 requires creation and advancement policy bindings while F005 owns Campaign policy state.
findings.decision: Campaign is the authority for policy IDs and versions; Character records persist exact bindings and historical receipts but cannot redefine Campaign policy.

findings.title: Character control ownership
findings.sourceIssue: F004 consumes control while F005 can mutate Character-control grants.
findings.decision: Character control is a Campaign-scoped grant controlled through F005 authority; F004 only validates and consumes the current grant.

findings.title: Character roster binding
findings.sourceIssue: Scene/Encounter preparation needs Character state without copying protected or mutable Character bodies.
findings.decision: Use stable Character ID, expected Character version, lifecycle state, controller decision, and a permission-safe roster projection or immutable roster snapshot.

findings.title: Definition and placement event overlap
findings.sourceIssue: F005 and F012 both define placement operations and similarly named Events.
findings.decision: Use domain-qualified aggregate and event envelopes (`scene.*`, `encounter.*`) while preserving source Definition immutability and placement-local identity.

findings.title: Launch snapshot versus live Character state
findings.sourceIssue: Characters may advance after a Scene is prepared or after a launch snapshot is created.
findings.decision: A launch snapshot binds exact Character versions. Later Character changes do not mutate an active Session; a new snapshot or governed amendment is required.

findings.title: Encounter attachment lifecycle
findings.sourceIssue: F012 can attach Encounter snapshots while F005 owns Scene validation and launch.
findings.decision: Attachment is a versioned Scene-local reference. Any changed dependency invalidates or warns on the attachment and requires Scene revalidation before a new launch snapshot.

findings.title: Player preview authority
findings.sourceIssue: F005 and F012 both support previews with hidden information risk.
findings.decision: Preview is a server-generated projection for a resolved subject/context; the client cannot choose a role or visibility class to widen access.

findings.title: Operation and Event naming normalization
findings.sourceIssue: The reviewed packets use compatible but domain-specific operation and Event vocabularies.
findings.decision: Preserve domain names, require common envelope fields (`operationId`, `aggregateId`, `expectedVersion`, `eventId`, `sequence`, `correlationId`), and prohibit cross-domain aliasing without migration.

findings.title: Recovery and migration order
findings.sourceIssue: Character, Scene, Encounter, attachment, and launch snapshots may all become stale after policy, pack, or schema change.
findings.decision: Migrate Campaign authority first, then Character, Scene, Encounter, attachment, and any new launch snapshot; historical snapshots remain immutable and explicitly incompatible when necessary.

findings.title: Fixture provenance boundary
findings.sourceIssue: The fixture package mixes source-backed selectors with synthetic workflow coverage.
findings.decision: Every fixture carries provenance class; synthetic fixtures are noncanonical and cannot establish source completeness or canonical content behavior.

findings.title: Diagnostics, export, and AI projection
findings.sourceIssue: Preparation state contains Player-private, GM-only, hidden Encounter, and source-license-sensitive fields.
findings.decision: All three surfaces consume separately authorized, pre-redacted projections; diagnostics default to exclude; AI has no authority; exports preserve provenance and redaction decisions.

findings.title: Implementation ordering
findings.sourceIssue: Parallel implementation could duplicate authority and persistence logic across Character, Campaign, Scene, Encounter, and Session services.
findings.decision: Implement shared IDs/authority/Event/recovery ports first, then Campaign authority and control, Character lifecycle, Scene/Encounter preparation, launch handoff, and finally the deterministic fixture harness.

nextReviewTrigger: Any downstream change that widens authority, changes canonical identity or version fields, alters launch snapshot immutability, changes fixture provenance, or changes the IA-D04-001 handoff.
